question: How does the game name and load the body file of a unit and its attachment pieces, and where is the civilization of the unit's player available while it does so?

scope.unitTypeRows: 0x82F700D8 + 0x94 * type, asset name at +0x20, member mask byte at +0x48
scope.limit: Static reading of the functions and tables named here. No unit creation or file load was observed. Functions and branches listed under limits were not read.

dependencies.use: Unit type rows start at 0x82F700D8 and are 0x94 bytes long.
The finding RVA-F-0330 in ai-options-boundaries.json records the function table 0x82138768 for the object at 0x8314F76C; 0x82D7FE40 is the word at 0x82138908 in that table.

typeRows.memberMask: Byte +0x48 of the row; bits 0, 1 and 2 select members in the group.

nameBuilder.callers: No direct caller was found. It is the word at 0x82138908, slot +0x1A0 of the function table 0x82138768. That table is the one recorded for the object at 0x8314F76C in ai-options-boundaries.json#/findings/RVA-F-0330/availabilityIndirectCallBoundary.
nameBuilder.arguments: r4 is a unit record kept in r30: signed byte +0x0 is the player, byte +0x1 is the unit type, and halfwords +0x1C and +0x1E are passed with the type to a log call. r5 is kept in r28.
nameBuilder.group: It allocates 0xE0 bytes and constructs the unit group with 0x82D99BB0(block, record), kept in r27. The constructor stores the function table 0x82135DB0 at word +0x0 and the record pointer at +0x84.
nameBuilder.startName: The name starts as the asset name at type row +0x20.
nameBuilder.type0: civ is the word at 0x830ECD28 + 4 * player. When civ is 0xF or less (unsigned), a 16 entry word table at 0x82D7FF20 (targets 0x82D7FF60 to 0x82D80014, 0xC apart) chooses one of 16 strings, from "settler_rom" for civ 0 to "settler_eng" for civ 0xF. Each is "settler_" plus a three letter code. The strings run from 0x82137950 to 0x82137A04.
nameBuilder.type0x1E: By the word at 0x830ECD08 + 4 * player: 2 gives "Great_General_Ind" (0x82D80078), 3 gives "Great_General_Mod" (0x82D8006C), any other value gives "GreatGeneral_Medieval" (0x82D80060).
nameBuilder.type0x1D: With that word equal to 3 the name is "Caravan_Mod" (0x82D800AC).
nameBuilder.type0x1F: "GreatSci_F" (0x82D800EC) when the byte at 0x82F6F2F0 + 0x23 * (word at 0x8312E670) is 0x19.
nameBuilder.otherTypes: No other type changes the name in this function. Types 2 and 7 keep "worker_rom_m".
nameBuilder.suffix: 0x82D80188..0x82D801D0: ".xml" (0x82123158) is appended unless ".kfm" (0x821322F8) is found in the name.
nameBuilder.call: 0x82D801D8..0x82D80208: indirect call through slot +0x14 of the group with r4 = the name and r5 = 0x200 when the low byte of r28 is 0, else 0. For type 0x18, bit 0x10 is added.

groupAndMembers.groupSlot0x14: In the group table 0x82135DB0, slot +0x14 is 0x82D9A110, a three instruction function that passes its r5 as r6 and -1 as r5 to 0x82D99EB8.
groupAndMembers.memberLoop: 0x82D99EB8..0x82D9A10C: type is the signed byte +0x1 of the record at group +0x84. For i = 0, 1, 2 (0x82D9A024..0x82D9A02C) it tests bit i of type row byte +0x48 (0x82D99F04..0x82D99F18). For a set bit it allocates 0xC0 bytes, constructs a member with 0x82D9B6E0(block, group, i) and calls member slot +0xB0 with r4 = the name, r5 = -1 and r6 = the flags (0x82D99F4C..0x82D99F68).
groupAndMembers.memberTable: Member table 0x82135C90: slot +0x14 is 0x82D9A1D8, +0x78 is 0x82D9B9F0, +0xB0 is 0x82D9A1C0 and +0xB4 is 0x82D9CF30. The function 0x82D9A1C0 sets r5 = -1 and jumps to slot +0xB4. The function 0x82D9A1D8 moves r5 to r6, sets r5 = -1 and jumps to slot +0xB0.
groupAndMembers.memberConstructor: 0x82D9B6E0 stores one register to bytes +0x89, +0x8A and +0x8B (0x82D9B7EC..0x82D9B7F4) and keeps the group pointer at +0x84.
groupAndMembers.secondRoute: The function 0x82D99CE8 (called at 0x82D81BDC) creates members for i = 3..8, testing bit (i mod 3) of the same row byte, and calls member slot +0x14 with r4 = the word at group +0x10 and r5 = 0. Its caller 0x82D81BA0(r3, r4, r5) copies the 0x54 byte record at 0x830F2BF0 + 0x54 * (256 * r4 + r5) and passes the word at record +0x3C as the group.

bodyLoadAndFallback.arguments: r31 = member, r27 = name, r26 = civ argument (-1 on the routes above), r30 = flags.
bodyLoadAndFallback.kfmBranch: A name with a ".kfm" match at an offset greater than 0 takes a separate branch that was not read (0x82D9D008).
bodyLoadAndFallback.test: 0x82D9D0E8..0x82D9D0F8: the name is tested with 0x82E80120. A nonzero low byte of the result skips the replacement. The function 0x82E80120 was not read.
bodyLoadAndFallback.replacement: 0x82D9D0FC..0x82D9D12C: otherwise the name is compared with "Numidian_Cavalry.xml" (0x82135B20) through 0x827F27B0. Equal: the name becomes "Knight.xml" (0x82135B38). Not equal: "Legion.xml" (0x8212FE54).
bodyLoadAndFallback.afterwards: The name is copied to member +0x10. The value (flags | 2) is stored at +0xA8 and bit 0x10000000 of word +0x4 is set. It calls 0x82D9C748(member, string, 1), then 0x82D9BE28(member, r26, string), 0x82D9C4B8 and 0x82C63820, and stores the low byte of r26 at +0x8C (0x82D9D1F0).

civilizationKey.arguments: r4 = civ argument, r5 = output string.
civilizationKey.civSource: When r4 is -1: player is the signed byte +0x0 of the record at +0x84 of the group at member +0x84; for a player in 0..7, civ is the word at 0x830ECD28 + 4 * player.
civilizationKey.clamp: A negative civ becomes 0 and a civ above 0xF becomes 0xF.
civilizationKey.nameTable: The name pointer is the word at 0x82F7A348 + 4 * civ, a table of 16 pointers to civilization name strings. 0x82D3C400(.., 0, 4) takes the first four characters and the result is copied to the output.
civilizationKey.codeTables: The table at 0x82F7A388 contains 16 entries of four bytes, each holding three ASCII characters and a terminator, from "rom" to "eng". No use of 0x82F7A388 was found in the functions read here. The table at 0x82F792F0 holds 16 pointers to strings with the same codes.

attachmentTable.test: 0x82D9C748(member, out, r5) copies the name at member +0x10, calls 0x821B4948(out, 0x5C), appends "_Attachments.xml" (0x82132300) with 0x821B2A60 and tests the result with 0x82E80120. When the test fails it sets out to the string at 0x8211EC34 and clears bit 0x10000000 of member word +0x4.
attachmentTable.read: 0x82D9C050 (called at 0x82D9CBF4) calls 0x82D9BE28 at 0x82D9C0CC. It opens the table with 0x82C92950(word at 0x8314F238, frame address, 9, name, 0, 0) at 0x82D9C0F4 and selects rows with the key "civ" (0x82135B8C) through 0x821D0BD0 at 0x82D9C13C. For a row it reads "file" (0x821229FC) and "bone" (0x82135B90) with 0x8230A118, then loads the file with 0x82C92950(.., 1, file, 0, 0) at 0x82D9C1EC.
attachmentTable.pieceCounts: For k = 0, 1, 2 it looks for "helmet" (0x82135B98), "weapon" (0x82135BA0) and "shield" (0x82128AA4) in the bone name with 0x827F1930 and stores (piece count - 1) to byte member +0x89 + k at 0x82D9C358.
attachmentTable.opener: 0x82C92950(r3, r4, r5, r6 = name, r7, r8) spans 0x82C92950..0x82C92C34. Its first instructions were read: it copies the name to a 0x104 byte frame string, calls 0x822D6270 and 0x821D6EC0(.., 0x5C) on it, and looks the result up with 0x822E9A38(r3 + 4, string). The rest was not read.

rowSelection.arguments: 0x82D9C050(r3 = member, r4 = civ argument, r5 = pointer to the table name string).
rowSelection.emptyName: 0x82D9C064..0x82D9C0A0: the table name is compared with the string at 0x8211EC34, which is empty in the image file. When they are equal the function returns at 0x82D9C3D8 with no load. 0x82D9C748 sets the name to that string when its test of the table file fails.
rowSelection.request: 0x82D9C0C0..0x82D9C0CC build the key string at frame +0x54 with 0x82D9BE28(member, r4, frame +0x54). 0x82D9C0D8..0x82D9C100 open the table; when the returned object word at frame +0x5C is 0 the function goes to its end at 0x82D9C3D0. 0x82D9C104..0x82D9C13C clear a result list at frame +0x84 (first), +0x88 (end) and +0x8C, and build a request that holds a pointer to that list, the string "civ" (0x82135B8C) and the key string pointer. It calls 0x821D0BD0(word +0x18 of the table object, request) at 0x82D9C13C.
rowSelection.walk: 0x821D0BD0..0x821D0C60(r3 = node, r4 = request): a zero node returns. At 0x821D0BEC..0x821D0C1C, when node word +0x14 is 1 and 0x82D32BA8(request + 4, node) returns a nonzero low byte, the node is appended to the list at request word +0x0 through 0x822E55F0. At 0x821D0C20..0x821D0C58 it takes each child in turn through 0x82307818(node, previous child or 0) and calls itself on the child at 0x821D0C40. Every node below the node it is given is visited, at any depth. Its direct callers are 0x82D9C13C and its own call at 0x821D0C40.
rowSelection.test: 0x82D32BA8..0x82D32C48(r3 = pointer to the pair (name, value), r4 = node): it calls slot +0x18 of the node, and a zero result returns 0. It reads the attribute named by the first word of the pair with 0x8230A118 and copies the result to a frame string with 0x821B2AD8. At 0x82D32C14..0x82D32C28 it compares that string with the second word of the pair through 0x827F27B0 and returns 1 when the compare returns 0, else 0. Its one direct caller is 0x821D0C04.
rowSelection.compare: 0x827F27B0..0x827F2800, 21 instructions: it compares two strings byte by byte to the end of the second string. Where two bytes differ, each byte in 0x41..0x5A gets bit 0x20 set and the bytes are compared again. It returns the last difference, and 0 when the strings match to the terminator.
rowSelection.attributeRead: 0x8230A118 looks the name up in the container at +0x44 of its first argument through 0x82308B48. A found entry returns a pointer to its text. No entry returns 0 (0x8230A178..0x8230A17C, 0x8230A1DC).
rowSelection.noCollectedNode: 0x82D9C140..0x82D9C150: when first equals end, the function goes to 0x82D9C3B8, which frees the list when it is not 0 and ends. No piece is loaded and no byte +0x89 to +0x8B is stored on that path. There is no default row in this function.
rowSelection.collectedNodes: 0x82D9C198..0x82D9C3B0: otherwise a loop runs over the list, four bytes per entry. For each entry it calls slot +0x18 of the entry's object, reads "file" and "bone" from the result with 0x8230A118 and loads the file with 0x82C92950. When that returns a zero low byte or leaves the object word 0, it goes to the next entry (0x82D9C1F0..0x82D9C204). For a loaded piece it appends the piece to the list at member +0x70 (0x82D9C208..0x82D9C214). For k = 0, 1, 2 it looks for the word of that k in the bone string with 0x827F1930. At the first k that is found it stores (count of the list at member +0x70) - 1 to member byte +0x89 + k and leaves the k loop (0x82D9C2C4..0x82D9C358). A later node whose piece loads overwrites a byte when that byte's word is the first of the three found in its bone string.
rowSelection.keyStrings: The key is the first four characters of the civilization name string at the pointer 0x82F7A348 + 4 * civ. Examples: index 0 starts with "Roma" and index 0xF starts with "Engl".
rowSelection.callers: The one direct call of 0x82D9C050 is at 0x82D9CBF4, in the function that starts at 0x82D9C7F0. It passes the signed member byte +0x8C as the civ argument and the name from a call of 0x82D9C748 just before (0x82D9CBCC..0x82D9CBF4). 0x82D9C7F0 has no direct caller. Its address is the word at 0x82135CA8, which is slot +0x18 of the member table 0x82135C90.
rowSelection.result: 0x821D0BD0 collects each node of kind 1 whose "civ" attribute equals the whole four letter key, compared without regard to the case of ASCII letters. 0x82D9C050 attempts one piece load for each collected node; a load that fails skips the node. When no node is collected it loads nothing and stores nothing to member bytes +0x89 to +0x8B. Static reading.

interpretation: Interpretation: 0x82D7FE40 is the place where the body file of a unit is chosen, and the player and civilization are at hand there, since the settler switch uses them. A body of its own for the unit of one civilization and one type could be chosen at the same point, before ".xml" is appended.
Interpretation: 0x82E80120 tests whether a file exists, and "Legion.xml" is the stand-in body for a missing file.
Interpretation: the attachment pieces differ by civilization through the "civ" rows of "<name>_Attachments.xml", not through the body name.
Interpretation: 0x830ECD08 looks like an era per player, and the byte table at 0x82F6F2F0 looks like a value per leader that picks the female models.
Interpretation: the four nine word tables are one parent class and three child classes. The four word table at 0x8212FF9C is their base, since the destructor of the parent calls 0x821C79A0.
Interpretation: the three child classes look like model viewers that differ in how they name the file: by unit type (0x82DC4F68), and two other ways.
Interpretation: since no constructor was found, this code looks unused in this image.
Interpretation: the body name of a unit on the map does not pass through 0x82DC4F68.

Interpretation: a row of the attachment table belongs to one civilization through civ="Roma", civ="Chin" and so on, and letter case does not matter. A unit of a civilization with no row gets no attachment pieces and no default set.
Interpretation: nodes of kind 1 are XML elements, and the walk visits the whole document, so the nesting of the rows does not matter.

Interpretation: for a body of its own for Chinese or Spanish Archers, the pieces can be chosen with rows keyed "Chin" and "Span" in the attachment table of the body name the unit loads. A new body name needs its own "_Attachments.xml", or the unit has no pieces.
Interpretation: slot +0x18 is the step that runs once the body file of a member is loaded: it sets up the loaded body and then reads the attachment table.

Interpretation: 0x82C63820 loads at once when the file is already available or when a flag asks for it, and otherwise queues the load or leaves a placeholder and returns. The queued load is finished later through slot +0xA4.

Interpretation: because byte +0x8C is stored after the loader call, a body that loads at once inside 0x82C63820 on a first load reads the attachment table with -1, which selects the civilization of the unit's player. On the routes recorded the civ argument is -1 as well, so the result is the same.

Interpretation: for a body of its own for Chinese or Spanish Archers, the attachment table is read each time the body is loaded, on the same call path as the body, so no separate step has to be added for the pieces.

Interpretation: a zero low byte of r5 asks for the unit's group to be created without keeping its body in memory: the members are made, the load is tried or skipped, and what was loaded is released again.
Interpretation: the object at member +0x34 is the receiver of a background load; its slot +0x4 reports success or failure, and on success member slot +0xA4 finishes the load and calls slot +0x18.
Interpretation: 0x82D9B080 is the unload of a member: body object, attachment pieces and helper lists.

Interpretation: for Chinese or Spanish Archers with a body of their own, the attachment table is read on the load path, and a unit created with the zero low byte holds no body until some later load that was not found here.

conclusion: In the functions read here, 0x82D7FE40 builds the body file name from the asset name in the unit type row and appends ".xml" unless the name contains ".kfm", replacing the name by civilization for type 0 and by other words for types 0x1D, 0x1E, 0x1F and 0x20. The unit group creates up to three members, and each loads the file in 0x82D9CF30, which substitutes "Legion.xml" or "Knight.xml" when the test 0x82E80120 fails. The attachment table "<name>_Attachments.xml" is tested in 0x82D9C748 and read in 0x82D9C050, which selects rows by a four letter civilization key from 0x82D9BE28. The selection 0x821D0BD0 collects each node of kind 1 whose "civ" attribute equals the whole key, compared without regard to the case of ASCII letters, and 0x82D9C050 attempts one piece load for each collected node and loads nothing when none is collected. Slot +0x18 of the member table is called by 0x82C63820 at two sites, each after the word at member +0x14 is not 0, and by 0x82C631D0; two paths of 0x82C63820 return without calling it, and 0x82D9CF30 stores member byte +0x8C after its call of 0x82C63820. On the name builder route with a zero low byte of r5, 0x82D7FE40 passes flags 0x200, or 0x210 for type 0x18, and, after a group call that returns a nonzero low byte, calls 0x82D9B080 on each nonzero entry of the list at group +0x78 to +0x7C, which calls slot +0x0 of the object at member +0x14 and stores 0 there; a later load of such a member was not found. 0x82DC4F68 is slot +0x20 of the function table 0x8212FFD0. In the scans run, the addresses of the four nine word tables are stored in destructors and no constructor was found. The worker name functions are not established. Static reading.
